name: Open vSwitch (OVS)
what_it_is: Open vSwitch is a production-quality, multilayer software switch licensed under Apache 2.0, designed for virtual machine environments and supporting distribution across multiple physical servers. It provides extensible programmatic forwarding with a kernel module for high-performance flow-based switching alongside a fully userspace datapath option.
components: ovs-vswitchd — main switch daemon implementing switch functionality
ovsdb-server — lightweight database server providing configuration data to ovs-vswitchd
ovs-dpctl — tool for configuring the kernel module datapath
ovs-vsctl — utility for querying and updating switch configuration via OVSDB
ovs-appctl — command interface for sending commands to running OVS daemons
ovs-ofctl — OpenFlow switch and controller management utility
ovs-testcontroller — simple OpenFlow controller for testing (not for production)
kernel module — Linux kernel datapath for high-performance flow switching
tcpdump patch — adds OpenFlow message parsing to tcpdump
protocols: OVSDB (Open vSwitch Database Management Protocol) with C and Python bindings
LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) for NIC bonding
measurement: sFlow — sampled packet and interface statistics export
Traffic mirroring (port mirroring) — copy packets to a designated monitoring port
ovs-ofctl dump-flows — display current OpenFlow flow table entries
ovs-vsctl list — query OVSDB tables for interface and port statistics
configuration: OVSDB transactional database — primary configuration store with C and Python bindings
ovs-vsctl — command-line interface to add/remove bridges, ports, tunnels, and flows
ovs-ofctl — add/modify/delete OpenFlow flow entries and query switch state
ovs-appctl — runtime tuning of daemon parameters (e.g., log levels, revalidation)
QoS / policing — per-port quality-of-service and rate-limiting configuration via OVSDB
fault_injection: ovs-testcontroller — simple OpenFlow controller that can drop or redirect flows for testing scenarios
ovs-ofctl — can install drop rules, priority overrides, and table-miss entries to simulate faults
ovs-appctl ofproto/trace — traces a hypothetical packet through the pipeline without sending real traffic
modes: Kernel datapath mode — high-performance flow switching via Linux kernel module (default, production use)
Userspace datapath with DPDK — kernel-bypass forwarding using DPDK poll-mode drivers
Userspace datapath without DPDK — experimental mode on Linux using non-DPDK devices, with acknowledged performance cost
Standalone mode — ovs-vswitchd acts as a learning switch without an external OpenFlow controller
Controller mode — ovs-vswitchd delegates forwarding decisions to an external OpenFlow controller
constraints: Userspace datapath without DPDK is explicitly marked experimental and incurs significant performance cost compared to the kernel datapath
OpenFlow support is version 1.0 plus extensions — full OpenFlow 1.3/1.5 feature parity is not guaranteed for all features
The kernel module must match the running kernel version; mismatches require recompilation or use of the userspace datapath
OVSDB is the sole configuration interface — there is no REST API or gRPC interface natively; external controllers must speak OpenFlow or OVSDB
No built-in Docker Compose or containerized service definitions are provided in the upstream repository
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml or container orchestration files in the upstream repository
No native BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) mention in README (though supported in code)
No native RSTP or LLDP mention in README
No built-in REST API — management is exclusively via OVSDB and OpenFlow
No integrated traffic generation or load testing tooling
